newsitem.title: USA: SEC sues former Tower lawyer.
newsitem.headline: SEC sues former Tower lawyer.

text.p: The Securities and Exchange Commission filed a suit in Manhattan federal court Tuesday against Michael Rosoff, the former senior in-house lawyer for Tower Financial Services.

The suit alleges that as part of the inner circle of Tower's chief executive officer, Steve Hoffenberg, he participated in a "mammoth fraud" against the purchasers of $215 million in promissory notes before Tower declared bankruptcy in 1993.
The SEC claims that Rosoff knew of Tower's material overstatement of its revenues and participated in the preparation of false and misleading financial statements.
The SEC wants Rosoff to disclose what profits he made from the scheme, give them up and pay unspecified fines.
Rosoff did not immediately return a phone call requesting comment.
The suit said he helped write Note Offering Documents that stated that Note funds would be used to purchase accounts receivable, but knew that the money was not used that way, the suit said.

Instead, the SEC claims, the funds were used "to keep this Ponzi scheme running, i.e., to make monthly interest payments to Note purchasers and to pay Towers' lavish operating expenses, including, inter alia, Rosoff's salary."
Rosoff, 45, of Chappaqua, New York, received $600,000 in salary and bonuses from Tower in 1992, the suit said.

According to a suit filed in 1994 by Tower's bankruptcy trustee, the company, which collected unpaid medical bills, fabricated some of its accounts receivable by taking names out of a phone book and inventing medical claims to match.
The suit does not accuse Rosoff of involvement in the bond fraud that Tower is alleged to have committed.
